# Results — Study 528 (Labor-Hiring-Rate) on the real survivor basket

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). Signal: the Belo-Lin-Bazdresch
hiring rate HN = (N_t − N_{t-1}) / (0.5·(N_t + N_{t-1})), from a curated panel of 10-K
cover-page full-time-employee counts. Forward returns from Yahoo daily adjusted prices.
As-of **2026-06-27**.*

**Definition**:
- HN_t = (N_t − N_{t-1}) / (0.5·(N_t + N_{t-1}))  (higher = faster hirer; bounded in [−2, 2])

**Prediction (Belo-Lin-Bazdresch 2014)**: HIGH hiring → LOW future returns (the labor
analogue of the investment anomaly). We go **long low-hiring / short high-hiring** (g1 − g3).

**Execution lag (one)**: the hiring rate for fiscal year y drives a 12-month forward total
return that *begins 4 months after the fiscal-year-end* (when the 10-K — with its cover-page
headcount — is public) and is entered at the close 1 trading day later. A forward window is
used only if it has fully completed by the as-of date — no partial period is ever stamped.

**Universe**: a fixed 28-name large-cap **survivor** basket. **Survivorship-biased** — every
firm survived to 2026.

**Data note**: employee counts are **not** machine-readable. Firms report headcount as 10-K
cover-page narrative text, so SEC EDGAR companyfacts / companyconcept / frames return employee
figures for only a handful of filers (verified ~5–11 names market-wide carry the
`dei:EntityNumberOfEmployees` numeric tag), and yfinance exposes only a single current
snapshot. The hiring rate is therefore computed from a **curated panel of 10-K cover-page
headcounts** (FY2013–FY2024), hardcoded for reproducibility, with the latest column
sanity-anchored to the live yfinance `fullTimeEmployees` snapshot.

**Window**: 11 signal years (2014–2024), forecasting 12-month returns 2015–2026.

| Employee counts | Curated 10-K cover-page panel (FY2013–FY2024), no XBRL/API source exists |
| Prices | Yahoo Finance daily adjusted close |

| Avg names/year | 28 |

| FWD fingerprint | `d6fd3efee81e` |

**SURVIVORSHIP-BIAS WARNING**: the basket is large-cap names still trading in 2026.
Aggressive hirers that over-expanded and subsequently failed (or were acquired in distress)
are absent. All results are upper bounds on a live strategy.

## Tercile returns (hiring-rate low to high, 12-month forward)

| Tercile | Mean return | Sharpe | HAC t-stat | Hit rate |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **g1 (low hiring — disciplined)** | **+17.5%/yr** | +1.24 | +5.40 | 100% |
| g2 (mid hiring) | +16.0%/yr | +0.85 | +3.99 | 91% |
| **g3 (high hiring — aggressive)** | **+22.2%/yr** | +1.66 | +10.03 | 100% |
| Equal-weight market | +18.7%/yr | +1.36 | +7.16 | 100% |

The predicted ranking is **inverted**: the fast hirers (g3) earned *more* than the
disciplined hirers (g1), +22.2% vs +17.5%/yr.

## Long low-hiring / short high-hiring hedge (g1 − g3)

| Metric | Value |
|---|---|
| Mean annual return | **−4.68%/yr** |
| Sharpe ratio | −0.35 |
| HAC Newey-West t-stat | **−1.29** |
| Hit rate (positive years) | 45% (5/11 years) |
| n (years) | 11 |

The hedge has the *wrong sign* (the paper predicts a positive low-minus-high return) and is
not statistically distinguishable from zero (|t| < 2).

## Excess vs equal-weight market

| Arm | Excess return | HAC t-stat |
|---|--:|--:|
| Low-hiring (g1) | −1.2%/yr | −0.74 |
| High-hiring (g3) | +3.5%/yr | +1.56 |

## Placebo / label-shuffle null (1000 shuffles)

| Metric | Value |
|---|---|
| Real hedge mean | −4.68%/yr |
| Shuffle mean | +0.04%/yr |
| Shuffle std | 5.06%/yr |
| Placebo p (P[shuffle ≥ real]) | **0.805** |

The real hedge sits in the **left** tail of the shuffle null — it is *worse* than a randomly
relabelled signal 80% of the time, the opposite of a real positive anomaly.

## Random-portfolio null (500 draws/year)

| Metric | Value |
|---|---|
| Random-control mean | −0.20%/yr (zero in expectation) |
| Random-control std | 9.9%/yr |
| Low-hiring beats random draw | **48%** of 500×11yr draws (chance level) |

## Costs (gross vs net)

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Gross hedge | −4.68%/yr |
| Trading drag (10 bps × 2.0 turnover) | −0.20%/yr |
| Borrow drag (50 bps short leg) | −0.50%/yr |
| **Net hedge** | **−5.38%/yr** |

The already-negative gross hedge only worsens after costs and short borrow.

## Synthetic positive control (seed-robust, 25 seeds)

| Planted premium | Mean hedge | Mean HAC t |
|---|--:|--:|
| 0.00/yr (null) | −0.1%/yr | −0.15 |
| −0.06/yr | +13.0%/yr | +14.94 |
| −0.10/yr | +21.8%/yr | +25.00 |

The engine recovers a planted hiring effect with a large, seed-robust t-stat, and the null
behaves (t ≈ 0). The real-tape non-result (in fact, sign reversal) is therefore a statement
about the **market and the survivor basket**, not the method.

## Verdict

The predicted effect (fast hiring → low returns) is **absent — in fact inverted** on this
survivor basket. The long-low-hire / short-high-hire hedge earns **−4.68%/yr** with HAC
*t* = **−1.29** (wrong sign, |t| < 2). The placebo p = **0.805** (the real result sits in the
*left* tail of the label-shuffle null — worse than a coin-flip relabelling), the low-hiring
leg beats only **48%** of random same-size draws (chance), and the negative gross hedge falls
to **−5.38%/yr net** once costs and short borrow are charged. The fast-hiring tercile *out*-earned
the disciplined one (+22.2% vs +17.5%/yr).

The synthetic control proves the engine is faithful: planting a −6%/yr hiring effect yields
HAC *t* ≈ +15 (seed-robust over 25 seeds), and the null behaves (*t* ≈ 0). So the absence
(and sign reversal) on the real tape is a property of the market and the basket, not the
method.

Two honest reasons the academic anomaly does not appear here:

1. **Wrong universe.** Belo-Lin-Bazdresch (2014) estimate the hiring-rate factor on the broad
   Compustat cross-section of all US firms, where small and mid-caps — and the over-expanding
   firms that subsequently disappoint — dominate the spread. On 28 heavily-covered large caps
   the effect is thin, and the surviving fast hirers are exactly the productive growth names.
2. **Survivorship reversal.** On a survivor basket the high-hiring group is dominated by
   *successful* expanders — AI/semiconductor (NVDA), hyperscale (AMZN, GOOGL, MSFT, COST,
   UNH) — whose hiring tracked genuine demand. Their stocks *led* the period (note 2024:
   high-hire tercile +31%, but the low-hire winners — Apple, energy majors that *cut*
   headcount — ripped harder, +52.6%, exactly the year the hedge finally turned positive).

- **Signal — NONE** (hedge *t* = −1.29, wrong sign; placebo p = 0.81; beats 48% of random
  draws; literature supports the effect for a broad non-biased universe, not survivor
  large-caps).
- **Tradability — MIRAGE** (no positive gross edge; −5.38%/yr net after costs and borrow;
  nothing to trade — and shorting the high-hiring leg means shorting the AI/hyperscale winners).
- **Predicted sign (fast hiring → low returns)? — BUSTED** (the sign *reverses* on the survivor
  large-cap panel: fast hirers earned +22.2%/yr vs +17.5%/yr for disciplined hirers, the same
  fate as the capex investment channel in [Study 523](../523-investment-to-assets/)).
